title: The Problem
description: Climate issues and climate literacy resources from Bay Area Youth Conservation.

thesis.heading: Misbeliefs prevent forward motion in crafting viable solutions to climate change
thesis.lede: Climate literacy and action matter more now than ever. False information and misconceptions ultimately hinder our progress toward a sustainable future. How can we tackle issues that we do not fully understand?
thesis.body: The vast majority of the world agrees that something must be done to reduce global warming. 62% of Americans feel a personal duty to reduce the effects of climate change. However, global emissions has increased, with human-produced greenhouse gases rising 49% since 1990.

blockOne.heading: California's temperatures is rising due to increasing emissions of greenhouse gases
blockOne.body: According to the California Environmental Protection Agency, weather extremes are intensifying and has become more erratic. The increase in greenhouse gas emissions has led average air temperatures to increase by about 2.5 degrees F since 1895. As a result, a multitude of problems has arose. Hotter and drier conditions has led to the increase of reports of work-related heat illnesses tripling in the past 20 years along with the raise of deadly wildfires and wildfire smoke and a significant loss of California's glaciers.
